title: Overview: the big ideas
summary: The chapter's key concepts and how its sections fit together.

blocks.md: Welcome to **Failure Recovery** (Vol III). This overview gives you the chapter's big ideas before the section-by-section lessons. Read the claims once, flip the flashcards, then take the warm-up quiz: it is fine to miss questions here, the lessons that follow fill the gaps.

A durable record tells a restarted agent what it intended and what it observed, but the record does not change the world. A provisioning request whose reply was lost may have created a billed environment or nothing at all, and no amount of replay settles which. Restoring a workspace snapshot resets local files, while the remote environment the agent created keeps running and keeps charging. Recovery therefore begins where recording ends, with decisions made on incomplete evidence.

rows: An external service and the runtime log share no atomic commit, so an established effect is remediated only by a separately committed forward operation that restores declared postconditions, not the past.
A trajectory saga durably registers each effectful step's cleanup template before dispatch, not after the step returns, so a crash never leaves an effect without its compensator.
Recovery order is a DAG of admitted cleanup operations rather than a reverse stack, and an unresolved node blocks only its transitive dependents.
Transport retry, fresh proposal, feedback repair, compensation, and hold or escalate are chosen by evidence class first, then admission, then expected cost.
One bounded repair attempt beats immediate unwind-and-rebuild iff its measured success rate exceeds p* = C_repair / C_fallback, evaluated separately in time and dollars.

Reversibility is relative to a subsystem and a grant, so a plan is organized into compensable preparation, a single pivot, and owned follow-up duties, with every check that can precede the pivot hoisted ahead of it.

A looping trajectory is hyperactive, not dead, so a watchdog compares a declared task projection, verifier results, and repeated action-outcome pairs over a bounded window, and its window sets detection latency.

On suspicion, fail-safe defaults hold the trajectory at every dispatch boundary without the agent's cooperation while preregistered cleanup runs under a separate narrow grant until residual obligations settle.
Scoped circuit breakers, a single retry owner, and bulkheads bound three different quantities when many trajectories share one dependency.
